claims.text: The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01, and the driver cannot carry limb (b) or limb (c). The pickup zone class is AIRPORT, so the arrival radius under the fee schedule is 150 m and the continuous-dwell minimum is 480 seconds. The driver's own trace never brings him inside that radius: the derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count of 0 out of 67 driver fixes, and his closest approach to the pin across the whole trace is a minimum driver-track distance of 358.15 m. Limb (b) therefore fails outright, and limb (c) fails too, because the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 seconds against a 480 second requirement. With (b) and (c) both broken, the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-02 turns the driver's arrival into an arithmetic question, and the arithmetic fails him. The driver is deemed to have arrived only where the trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius with reported accuracy of 25 m or better. In the 15 minutes preceding the 11:41:50 cancellation the trace contains no in-radius fix at all — qualifying_fix_count 0, minimum driver-to-pin distance 358.15 m. The driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 8.00 fee recorded as charged in the fare breakdown.

POL-NS-06 supplies the cleanest route to judgment: state the minimum, state the measured dwell, state the shortfall. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds — the derived arrival block reports longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec of 0.0 and a shortfall_sec of 480.0 against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum. A full 480 second shortfall on an 8 minute waiting requirement means the cancellation fee of SGD 8.00 is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she answered messages.

The driver cannot rescue that shortfall by accumulating dwell across separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i). Limb (i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, covering the pickup road, with a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-00616-01 is MISSING: its payload is null, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. No advisory covers this road in this window, so limb (i) is unavailable and the shortfall stands. The absence of the advisory is itself the citable fact, and POL-GEN-02 fixes a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 so it can carry no fact for the driver either.

The driver's 'arrived' event at 11:33:52 is a false marker caught by POL-NS-05. The derived driver track is never closer than 358.15 m to the pin at any fix in the trace — more than the 300 m threshold — so at the arrival timestamp the driver was not at the pickup point and the waiting clock he started is void. On the recomputed basis no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip (qualifying_fix_count 0), so under POL-NS-05(ii) the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the referrals list.

Even taken purely on the driver's own side of the story, the pickup failed at the driver's end, and POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider. All three limbs hold on this record: at 11:34:40 the rider sent a locating message, 'we have 4 suitcases, pin is arrival door 4, please come down'; the driver's only message (11:34:20) preceded that message, he posted no reply within 120 seconds of it, and he made no in-app voice call at any point (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty); and the rider's own track keeps her at the pin throughout — rider_qualifying_fix_count 55 of 55 fixes, with a maximum rider-track distance of 17.14 m, far inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius. The fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's own statement places him at departures while the pin is the arrival pick-up bay, and the derived track never brings him closer than 358.15 m to the pin — outside the 150 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets. His account is that he held and waited before cancelling, which the trip record reflects as wait_time_min of 8.0 against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum. On that route POL-NS-03 resolves the case the same way: the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded to the rider in full. Because the rider named the arrival door in chat and the driver nonetheless cancelled from departures, limb (i) allocates the loss to the driver and no compensation is payable.

There is no impairment discount to apply, so the ruling should be the full refund and not the partial refund that POL-NS-08 confines a case to. The GPS trace is complete on its face — coverage_pct 100.0, point_count 67, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, sample_interval_sec 10.0 against an expected 10.0 — and its admissibility block carries no issues and a weight_multiplier of 1.0, so no POL-NS-08 limb (a), (b) or (c) is engaged. The only artifact below full weight is the absent advisory at 0.0, which the rider cites for its absence and not for its content, and which carries no deciding fact. The arrival arithmetic therefore runs on clean, full-weight evidence.

claims.text: The driver's termination satisfies two of the four limbs of POL-NS-01 on its own terms: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-16T11:33:52+08:00 (limb (a)), and the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - and not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which would have been the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. The driver told the truth in the reason code, and the policy says a driver who does so should not be penalised for the word he chose.

This is a diligent driver who bore a real cost, not a fee-farmer: he accepted the job at 11:30:40, marked arrival at 11:33:52 (time_to_arrival_min 3.2), and did not cancel until 11:41:50 - wait_time_min 8.0, the full AIRPORT waiting period - after driving out to Changi. POL-NS-07 exists precisely so that a driver who drove to Changi and waited the clock through has that cost said in cash rather than merely being told he loses nothing.

The anti-farming guard in POL-NS-07 does not trip and cannot be turned against this driver: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4 or more, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.009, below the threshold of greater than 0.08. The check is conjunctive and neither limb is met, so no escalation lies under POL-NS-09(d) on this ground and no adverse inference about this driver's termination history is available.

The driver's own trace places his closest recorded approach to the pickup pin at 358.15 m - outside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius, but inside the 400 m ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets for a wrong-entrance arrival. This is therefore the wrong-face-of-the-venue case that POL-NS-03 governs, not a driver who never came near the pickup, and both the fault allocation and the driver's compensation must be decided under POL-NS-03 rather than under a bare 'he never arrived'.

On POL-NS-03's fault allocation the mislocation should be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver paid the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the cancellation fee (SGD 4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider). Changi T1 registers 4 separate pickup points (registered_pickup_points 4), and the rider's own message names 'arrival door 4' while the registered pin label on this trip is 'Arrival Pick-up Bay 3' - so the record does not establish that the rider ever stated the correct entrance within the meaning of POL-NS-03(i), and where no sub-location matching the registered pickup point was specified by either party the policy directs that the mislocation be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, which is limb (ii).

Honest concession on the fee itself: the driver does not contend that the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee can stand, because his trace contains no qualifying fix inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius (qualifying_fix_count 0) and no in-geofence dwell at all (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0 against the 480 s AIRPORT minimum), so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) are not met and the fee is not chargeable. The driver's case is about fault allocation and his compensation, not about his keeping the fee.

The amount charged is not overstated and there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): SGD 8.00 is exactly the figure POL-NS-01's resolution rule produces - the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) - and the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line reconciles with it to the cent, so nothing in this dispute turns on the figure the rider was charged.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee charged for trip TRP-00616 is refunded in full to the rider. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions in POL-NS-01 hold. Two do: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 11:33:52 and the trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW (limbs (a) and (d)). Two do not. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00616 records 0 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius and the driver's closest recorded approach to the pin is 358.15 m, so there is no continuous in-geofence dwell at all against the 480 s the AIRPORT zone class requires (limbs (b) and (c)). The fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 (measured dwell 0 s against the 480 s minimum, shortfall 480 s). The driver's 'arrived' marker at 11:33:52 was set while he was at least 358.15 m from the pin — more than the 300 m threshold — so under POL-NS-05 the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix leaves nothing to compute from, because the trace contains no such fix anywhere in the trip; POL-NS-05(ii) therefore applies and directs that a false-arrival event be recorded against the driver, which I do in the referrals. The 'wait_time_min 8.0' the driver relies on is measured from that false marker and does not show a compliant wait. No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not; the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against 110 completed trips, a rate of 0.009), but that only removes a bar to payment, it does not create one. POL-NS-03 does not assist the driver: a driver whose closest approach is 358.15 m and who marks arrival from beyond 300 m is a false-marker case under POL-NS-05, not a wrong-face-of-the-same-venue case, and in any event the rider's 11:34:40 message ('pin is arrival door 4, please come down') did identify the pick-up location while the driver remained at departures, so the mislocation is not attributable to pin ambiguity. The rider is also exonerated on POL-NS-04: the rider sent a locating message, the driver neither replied within 120 s nor placed an in-app call, and the rider's device stayed within 17.14 m of the pin across 55 of 55 qualifying fixes, inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius. On weight (POL-GEN-02): every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the GPS trace and the trip record — is at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below that, and no POL-NS-08 limb (clock skew, trace gap, chat truncation, fare mismatch) is engaged. The fare line reconciles: SGD 8.00 is the GREATER of the SGD 6.00 AIRPORT zone-class fee and the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00616-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0; it is cited only for its absence and carries no fact, so it neither lowers confidence nor makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation available. Amounts used: contested cancellation fee SGD 8.00; refund to the rider SGD 8.00; driver compensation none.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 8.00 no-show fee is refunded in full. To the driver: the fee cannot stand, and no compensation is payable.

The fee (POL-NS-01). All four conditions must hold together. Limbs (a) and (d) are met - the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 11:33:52 and the driver terminated with RIDER_NO_SHOW, not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. Limbs (b) and (c) fail: the GPS trace never places the driver inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius (0 qualifying fixes out of 67; minimum driver-to-pin distance 358.15 m), so there is no qualifying in-geofence fix and no in-geofence dwell (0.0 s against the 480 s airport minimum, shortfall 480 s). The fee is not chargeable (POL-NS-02; POL-NS-06). The figure itself is correct - SGD 8.00 is exactly the POL-NS-01 resolution-rule maximum of the SGD 6.00 AIRPORT zone fee and the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL tier fee - so the whole SGD 8.00 is returned.

Rider exoneration (POL-NS-04). At 11:34:40 the rider sent a locating message ('we have 4 suitcases, pin is arrival door 4, please come down'). The driver's only message (11:34:20) preceded it; he posted no reply within 120 seconds of it and logged no in-app call before cancelling. The rider's own track stays within 17.14 m of the pin at most, across 55 of 55 qualifying fixes, well inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius. All three limbs hold, so the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

False arrival (POL-NS-05). The 11:33:52 marker was set while the trace places the driver at least 358.15 m from the pin - beyond the 300 m limit - and after recomputation the trip contains no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere. POL-NS-05(ii) therefore directs the full refund, no compensation, and a referral recording a false-arrival event against the driver.

The driver's claims. POL-NS-03: the 358.15 m approach is inside that clause's 400 m ceiling, but the 300 m line in POL-NS-05 puts this on the false-marker side rather than the wrong-entrance side; and POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill requires that neither party specified a sub-location, whereas the rider named the arrival door and the driver did not move to it (POL-NS-03(i)). The requested SGD 4.00 goodwill is declined, and both POL-NS-04 and POL-NS-05(ii) state that no driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensation is unavailable because it requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, which it is not. The anti-farming guard does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 is below 4; 1/110 = 0.009 is below 0.08), so there is no POL-NS-09(d) escalation - but that creates no payment either. The driver's concession that the fee cannot stand is accepted and agrees with the arithmetic above.

The rider's POL-NS-06(i) point. No traffic advisory covers the pickup road in this window (EV-ADVIS-00616-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so separate in-geofence intervals may not be summed and the 480 s shortfall stands.

Confidence and integrity. No POL-NS-08 limb is engaged: the trace is complete (100% coverage, 67 fixes, no gap, 2 s agreement between the arrived event and the nearest fix), the chat log reconciles with the trip record (2 = 2), and the SGD 8.00 fare line matches the fee schedule. The only sub-weight artifact is the MISSING advisory at 0.0, which is cited for its absence only and carries no deciding fact, so it does not cap confidence (POL-GEN-02(2)). The deciding facts rest on weight-1.0 artifacts - the GPS trace and the trip record - so the confidence cap is 1.0.

Basis of amounts: SGD 8.00 cancellation fee charged (EV-FARE-00616), refunded in full; driver compensation none.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your account is supported and the SGD 8.00 is refunded in full. To the driver: your account of waiting does not survive the trace, and no compensation is payable.

The fee cannot stand. POL-NS-01 requires the driver to have been inside the 150 m airport pickup geofence at or before the 'arrived' event and to have held position there for 480 seconds. The GPS trace contains no in-geofence fix at all — qualifying fixes 0 of 67 — and the driver's closest recorded approach to the pin was 358.15 m, so limbs (b) and (c) both fail. POL-NS-02 (no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation) and POL-NS-06 (dwell 0 s against the 480 s AIRPORT minimum, a 480 s shortfall) each refund the SGD 8.00. The amount itself is correct: the fee schedule takes the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), and the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line (SGD 8.00) reconciles to the cent, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

The driver's 'arrived' marker at 11:33:52 was set more than 300 m from the pin — his minimum distance across the whole trace is 358.15 m — so under POL-NS-05 the marker is FALSE and starts no waiting clock. Recomputed, no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) refunds the fee in full, bars driver compensation, and requires the false-arrival event to be recorded; that is the referral below.

Driver's claims. I accept that the trip record carries an 'arrived' event (limb (a)) and a RIDER_NO_SHOW termination with no boarding event (limb (d)), and that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 is below 4; 1/110 = 0.009 is below 0.08), so no POL-NS-09(d) escalation lies. But limbs (a) and (d) alone do not make the fee chargeable: (b) and (c) fail, so POL-NS-01 is not satisfied and POL-NS-07 — which needs POL-NS-01 in full before it pays 80% (SGD 6.40 of SGD 8.00) — pays nothing. I reject the POL-NS-03 routing and its goodwill request. POL-NS-03 reaches a wrong-face arrival only where the driver was stationary for the required dwell within 400 m, and the line between it and POL-NS-05 is the 300 m mark; a driver who marks arrival 358.15 m away is caught by the false-marker clause, not the wrong-entrance clause. Independently, POL-NS-03's own precondition fails: the recorded window from the arrival tap to the cancellation (11:33:52 to 11:41:50) is 478 seconds, short of the 480 second AIRPORT dwell. The POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill claim fails on its wording as well: limb (ii) applies only where NEITHER party specified a sub-location, and the rider's 11:34:40 message specified 'arrival door 4'. And POL-NS-05(ii) states in terms that no compensation is payable where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists. The driver's honest concession that the fee is not chargeable is correct, and his observation that the fare reconciles is correct but does not change the outcome.

Rider's claims. I accept the arrival and dwell analysis (POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) fail; POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 give the full SGD 8.00 refund). I accept that dwell cannot be accumulated under POL-NS-06(i): the traffic advisory is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and a MISSING artifact carries no fact for either side. I accept POL-NS-04: the rider's 11:34:40 message was locating, the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of it and made no in-app call (in_app_calls empty), and the rider's own fixes place her within the 200 m AIRPORT presence radius throughout (55 of 55 fixes, maximum 17.14 m). I accept POL-NS-05, and I reach the no-compensation result through it rather than through POL-NS-03, which does not govern on these facts.

No driver compensation is payable, the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and the fee is not held. POL-NS-09 is not engaged: every artifact that carries a deciding fact is at full weight 1.0, confidence is above the 0.70 floor, neither profile shows a qualifying repeat-dispute or abuse pattern, and POL-NS-05 resolves the position conflict rather than leaving it open.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee recorded in the fare breakdown is refunded to the rider in full. Why the fee cannot stand. This was an AIRPORT pickup, so the rules require the driver to hold inside a 150 m arrival radius for at least 480 seconds. The GPS trace — 67 fixes, no gaps, admitted at full weight — never places the driver inside that radius: 0 qualifying in-radius fixes out of 67, and his closest recorded approach to the pin is 358.15 m. The longest continuous hold inside the radius is 0 seconds against the 480-second minimum, a shortfall of 480 seconds. POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) therefore fail and the fee is not chargeable; POL-NS-06 gives the refund, and POL-NS-02 reaches the same result because there is no qualifying in-radius fix at all. The rider's POL-NS-04 claim (she sent a locating message at 11:34:40 — 'we have 4 suitcases, pin is arrival door 4, please come down' — the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds and made no in-app call, and her device stayed within 17.14 m of the pin across all 55 rider fixes) supports the same refund and is accepted; it adds no compensation either way. The 'arrived' tap at 11:33:52 is a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: the driver is never closer than 358.15 m at any point (over the 300 m threshold), and the trace shows him travelling at 28–30 km/h rather than holding. Recomputing the waiting clock from the first qualifying in-radius fix gives no such fix anywhere in the trip, so under POL-NS-05(ii) the fee is refunded, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver (see referrals). For the driver. I accept limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 — there is an 'arrived' event and the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three recognised — and that the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 1, and 1/110 = 0.009, both below threshold), so no escalation arises on that ground. But POL-NS-07 compensation requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and limbs (b) and (c) fail, so no compensation is payable however real the wait felt, and the trip record's wait_time_min of 8.0 cannot substitute for the missing geofence hold. Your POL-NS-03 arguments also fail: POL-NS-03 needs the trace to show you stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and the trace shows you moving at about 28–30 km/h; and in any event the rider did name a where-to-find point ('arrival door 4') in the chat, which would place the loss on the driver rather than on pin ambiguity, so the SGD 4.00 pin-ambiguity goodwill is not payable. You are also right that the SGD 8.00 figure itself is sound — it is the greater of the AIRPORT zone fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) — but a correctly computed fee that is not chargeable is still refunded. Integrity. POL-NS-08 raises no defect: the SGD 8.00 line reconciles exactly with the fee schedule, the trace has no gaps and includes the rider track, and the chat log is complete at 2 messages matching the trip record. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00616-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, which is why no dwell can be accumulated across intervals under POL-NS-06(i); its absence supports rather than defeats the refund. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

ledger.claim: The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01, and the driver cannot carry limb (b) or limb (c). The pickup zone class is AIRPORT, so the arrival radius under the fee schedule is 150 m and the continuous-dwell minimum is 480 seconds. The driver's own trace never brings him inside that radius: the derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count of 0 out of 67 driver fixes, and his closest approach to the pin across the whole trace is a minimum driver-track distance of 358.15 m. Limb (b) therefore fails outright, and limb (c) fails too, because the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 seconds against a 480 second requirement. With (b) and (c) both broken, the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-02 turns the driver's arrival into an arithmetic question, and the arithmetic fails him. The driver is deemed to have arrived only where the trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius with reported accuracy of 25 m or better. In the 15 minutes preceding the 11:41:50 cancellation the trace contains no in-radius fix at all — qualifying_fix_count 0, minimum driver-to-pin distance 358.15 m. The driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 8.00 fee recorded as charged in the fare breakdown.

POL-NS-06 supplies the cleanest route to judgment: state the minimum, state the measured dwell, state the shortfall. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds — the derived arrival block reports longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec of 0.0 and a shortfall_sec of 480.0 against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum. A full 480 second shortfall on an 8 minute waiting requirement means the cancellation fee of SGD 8.00 is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she answered messages.

The driver cannot rescue that shortfall by accumulating dwell across separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i). Limb (i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, covering the pickup road, with a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-00616-01 is MISSING: its payload is null, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. No advisory covers this road in this window, so limb (i) is unavailable and the shortfall stands. The absence of the advisory is itself the citable fact, and POL-GEN-02 fixes a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 so it can carry no fact for the driver either.

The driver's 'arrived' event at 11:33:52 is a false marker caught by POL-NS-05. The derived driver track is never closer than 358.15 m to the pin at any fix in the trace — more than the 300 m threshold — so at the arrival timestamp the driver was not at the pickup point and the waiting clock he started is void. On the recomputed basis no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip (qualifying_fix_count 0), so under POL-NS-05(ii) the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the referrals list.

Even taken purely on the driver's own side of the story, the pickup failed at the driver's end, and POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider. All three limbs hold on this record: at 11:34:40 the rider sent a locating message, 'we have 4 suitcases, pin is arrival door 4, please come down'; the driver's only message (11:34:20) preceded that message, he posted no reply within 120 seconds of it, and he made no in-app voice call at any point (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty); and the rider's own track keeps her at the pin throughout — rider_qualifying_fix_count 55 of 55 fixes, with a maximum rider-track distance of 17.14 m, far inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius. The fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's own statement places him at departures while the pin is the arrival pick-up bay, and the derived track never brings him closer than 358.15 m to the pin — outside the 150 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets. His account is that he held and waited before cancelling, which the trip record reflects as wait_time_min of 8.0 against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum. On that route POL-NS-03 resolves the case the same way: the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded to the rider in full. Because the rider named the arrival door in chat and the driver nonetheless cancelled from departures, limb (i) allocates the loss to the driver and no compensation is payable.

There is no impairment discount to apply, so the ruling should be the full refund and not the partial refund that POL-NS-08 confines a case to. The GPS trace is complete on its face — coverage_pct 100.0, point_count 67, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, sample_interval_sec 10.0 against an expected 10.0 — and its admissibility block carries no issues and a weight_multiplier of 1.0, so no POL-NS-08 limb (a), (b) or (c) is engaged. The only artifact below full weight is the absent advisory at 0.0, which the rider cites for its absence and not for its content, and which carries no deciding fact. The arrival arithmetic therefore runs on clean, full-weight evidence.

ledger.claim: The driver's termination satisfies two of the four limbs of POL-NS-01 on its own terms: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-16T11:33:52+08:00 (limb (a)), and the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - and not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which would have been the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. The driver told the truth in the reason code, and the policy says a driver who does so should not be penalised for the word he chose.

This is a diligent driver who bore a real cost, not a fee-farmer: he accepted the job at 11:30:40, marked arrival at 11:33:52 (time_to_arrival_min 3.2), and did not cancel until 11:41:50 - wait_time_min 8.0, the full AIRPORT waiting period - after driving out to Changi. POL-NS-07 exists precisely so that a driver who drove to Changi and waited the clock through has that cost said in cash rather than merely being told he loses nothing.

The anti-farming guard in POL-NS-07 does not trip and cannot be turned against this driver: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4 or more, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.009, below the threshold of greater than 0.08. The check is conjunctive and neither limb is met, so no escalation lies under POL-NS-09(d) on this ground and no adverse inference about this driver's termination history is available.

The driver's own trace places his closest recorded approach to the pickup pin at 358.15 m - outside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius, but inside the 400 m ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets for a wrong-entrance arrival. This is therefore the wrong-face-of-the-venue case that POL-NS-03 governs, not a driver who never came near the pickup, and both the fault allocation and the driver's compensation must be decided under POL-NS-03 rather than under a bare 'he never arrived'.

On POL-NS-03's fault allocation the mislocation should be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver paid the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the cancellation fee (SGD 4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider). Changi T1 registers 4 separate pickup points (registered_pickup_points 4), and the rider's own message names 'arrival door 4' while the registered pin label on this trip is 'Arrival Pick-up Bay 3' - so the record does not establish that the rider ever stated the correct entrance within the meaning of POL-NS-03(i), and where no sub-location matching the registered pickup point was specified by either party the policy directs that the mislocation be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, which is limb (ii).

Honest concession on the fee itself: the driver does not contend that the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee can stand, because his trace contains no qualifying fix inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius (qualifying_fix_count 0) and no in-geofence dwell at all (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0 against the 480 s AIRPORT minimum), so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) are not met and the fee is not chargeable. The driver's case is about fault allocation and his compensation, not about his keeping the fee.

The amount charged is not overstated and there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): SGD 8.00 is exactly the figure POL-NS-01's resolution rule produces - the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) - and the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line reconciles with it to the cent, so nothing in this dispute turns on the figure the rider was charged.
